summary.text: Proteins are large biomolecules made of one or more long chains of amino acid residues.
They catalyse metabolic reactions, provide structure to cells and organisms, transport molecules, and respond to stimuli.
A protein's amino acid sequence is dictated by its gene, and it usually folds into a specific 3D structure that determines its activity.

facts.label: Building blocks
facts.value: Amino acid residues joined by peptide bonds

facts.label: Standard amino acids
facts.value: The genetic code specifies 20 of them

facts.label: Named in 1838
facts.value: Described by Mulder, named by Berzelius

facts.label: Urease
facts.value: Shown to be a protein by Sumner in 1926

items.prompt: A lab makes a chain of 15 amino acid residues. What would it usually be called?

options.label: A protein, since any chain of amino acids counts
A peptide, since short chains are rarely considered proteins
A cofactor, since it is smaller than a protein
A proteasome, since it is a short assembly

items.explain: Short polypeptides of fewer than 20 to 30 residues are rarely considered proteins and are commonly called peptides.

items.prompt: A cell makes a protein that folds wrongly. What usually happens to it?

options.label: It lasts as long as a normal protein, since lifespan is fixed
It is turned into a cofactor for other proteins
It is exported whole to be rebuilt outside the cell
It is degraded more rapidly than normal, often by the proteasome

items.explain: Abnormal or misfolded proteins are degraded more rapidly, often by the proteasome.

items.prompt: Two proteins are made from genes with different nucleotide sequences. Why would they likely work differently?

options.label: Their amino acid sequences differ, which usually changes how they fold into 3D shapes
Genes decide only how long a protein lasts, not its makeup
Their genes change how many peptide bonds a cell can break
Different genes make different cofactors but identical proteins

items.explain: A protein's amino acid sequence is dictated by its gene, and the sequence usually results in folding into a specific 3D structure that determines its activity.

items.prompt: An enzyme works only when a metal ion is bound to it. What is this helper called?

options.label: A peptide
A proteasome
A cofactor
A polypeptide

items.explain: Proteins that require a non-protein chemical compound or ion for biological activity use what are known as cofactors.

items.prompt: Why do animals need protein in their diet?

options.label: It supplies essential amino acids that the body cannot make
It is copied directly into muscle without being broken down
It is needed only to be burned for energy
It keeps cofactors topped up in every cell

items.explain: Dietary protein is digested into amino acids; essential ones cannot be made by animals, and the pool is mostly used to make new body proteins.

items.prompt: In the 1800s, Mulder found that nearly all proteins shared one empirical formula. What did he wrongly conclude?

options.label: That proteins are made of sugars joined in chains
That proteins might be one single type of very large molecule
That each protein needs its own unique element
That proteins cannot be broken into smaller products

items.explain: Mulder concluded, erroneously, that proteins might be composed of a single type of very large molecule.
